# Winifred Tolley

## Overview

- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v1 c25 P46](../source/v01-c25.md#nw-v01-c25-p0046)</sub>
- **Status:** Married  <sub>[v4 c37 P0](../source/v04-c37.md#nw-v04-c37-p0000), [v4 c37 P5](../source/v04-c37.md#nw-v04-c37-p0005)</sub>
- **Origin:** St. Brendan's Island  <sub>[v1 c2 P2](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0002), [v2 c6 P0](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0000)</sub>
- **Role:** Housekeeper and seamstress  <sub>[v1 c25 P25](../source/v01-c25.md#nw-v01-c25-p0025), [v2 c8 P13](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0013)</sub>
- **Titles:** Miss Winifred; Miss Tolley; Mrs. Ambrose Kerr  <sub>[v4 c37 P0](../source/v04-c37.md#nw-v04-c37-p0000)</sub>

## Appearance

Winifred is a stout woman with a healthy, round, pink-and-white complexion and cheerful brown eyes. She wears a large black straw hat adorned with yellow ribbon bows, fastened securely under her rigid, tiny bun with an elastic band, along with bleached black lace mits. She takes pride in her appearance, wearing stylish dresses with ruffles and frills for special occasions.

_Sources: [v1 c25 P25](../source/v01-c25.md#nw-v01-c25-p0025), [v1 c25 P28](../source/v01-c25.md#nw-v01-c25-p0028), [v2 c6 P3](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0003), [v2 c6 P4](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0004), [v2 c8 P3](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0003)_

## Personality

Winifred is sharp-tongued, extremely candid, and deeply opinionated, often expressing strong disdain for men, Methodists, and foolish behavior. Beneath her caustic and sarcastic exterior, she possesses a fiercely compassionate heart and a readiness to help those in need, particularly children and suffering neighbors. She is highly practical, industrious, and takes great pride in her skill as a needlewoman.

_Sources: [v1 c25 P30](../source/v01-c25.md#nw-v01-c25-p0030), [v1 c25 P41](../source/v01-c25.md#nw-v01-c25-p0041), [v1 c28 P31](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0031), [v2 c6 P24](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0024)_

## History

Winifred lived for decades as an unmarried woman in her green-painted house on the Seven Gulls road, known throughout the area for her blunt speech, her expert sewing skills, and her willingness to care for sick neighbors. She regularly attended Presbyterian services and frequently voiced her distaste for Methodists and men. She developed a close friendship with Nell Harcourt, whom she supported during her years as a teacher and throughout her marriage to Dr. Hugh Carrow. When Lorna Vane was left in hardship, Winifred actively advocated for her and helped arrange for a paying boarder to stay at her cottage. In her late fifties, after years of rejecting suitors and insisting she would never marry, she surprised her friends by accepting the proposal of her long-time admirer, Ambrose Kerr, and getting married.

_Sources: [v1 c25 P25](../source/v01-c25.md#nw-v01-c25-p0025), [v1 c25 P36](../source/v01-c25.md#nw-v01-c25-p0036), [v2 c6 P24](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0024), [v2 c8 P3](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0003), [v4 c37 P0](../source/v04-c37.md#nw-v04-c37-p0000), [v4 c37 P5](../source/v04-c37.md#nw-v04-c37-p0005)_

## Background by volume

- Had a single brother who died young around the age of twenty  <sub>[v3 c19 P28](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0028)</sub>
- Lived as a lifelong single woman in Seven Gulls before marrying later in life  <sub>[v4 c37 P0](../source/v04-c37.md#nw-v04-c37-p0000)</sub>

## Quotes

> I’m not trying to dishearten you, Nell, because your notion might hold value... nevertheless, managing your school will keep you completely occupied, so my friendly counsel is to leave these improvements alone, that’s what.  <sub>[v2 c1 P54](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0054)</sub>

> You fail to understand how it feels when two large girls come leaping directly onto you, rousing you from a deep slumber following an extensive and exhausting voyage.  <sub>[v1 c19 P85](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0085)</sub>

> I would prefer to exist for fifty rational years instead of a hundred senseless ones.  <sub>[v1 c19 P66](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0066)</sub>

> A person can easily catch rheumatism in her legs, Nell. However, solely the elderly ought to experience soul rheumatism. Fortunately, I have escaped it entirely.  <sub>[v2 c25 P10](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0010)</sub>

> If you can’t shine like an electric star, shine like a candlestick.  <sub>[v1 c26 P25](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0025)</sub>
